text: hm. this is doing the same kinda painting problems i have had before [Image #1] and i was hoping that, for example, i turn on wireframe, and see how this is a face, i could click inside of here and it fills [Image #2] oh which if i zoom in, it is doing that! it just, the hit testing on it or something is off.
resolution: Fixed the paint hit-testing scatter on real meshes. The render culls back-faces (cull_mode=.back) but the paint raycast did not, so on a thin/curved scanned mesh (the user's humanoid) dragging let the ray pick whichever triangle was geometrically nearest — flipping between the visible near face and the invisible far/inside face — which paints 'through' the surface and reads as scattered/offset. model_paint.pick now prefers the nearest FRONT-facing hit (geometric normal opposing the ray) with a nearest-any fallback so a mis-wound model still paints. Proved the underlying ray math + viewport capture are exactly correct via a new env-gated headless probe (RJIT_PAINTPROBE) that paints known viewport pixels: center pixel hits the center face, off-center pixels hit the correct neighbours (vp 1280x800, center->143, right->145, left->146). The clean convex car never showed the bug (its visible faces were already front-facing), which is why only a real mesh triggered it. Asked the user to retest on their model; if any residual cursor offset remains it would be a live point-vs-pixel viewport mismatch, and RJIT_PAINTPROBE prints the live vp dims to pinpoint it.
